prompt.context: If you have been reading the newspaper lately, you have seen the news about Starbucks and how terribly the company has been doing lately. Starbucks has had no growth and is facing competition from Dunkin Donuts, which has partnered with Baskin Robbins at many of its locations.
prompt.question: Starbucks is our client. Do you think that they should add ice cream to their retail stores?

framework: Customers: compare Starbucks vs. Dunkin Donuts demographics, income levels, purpose and timing of visit
Starbucks differentiation: assess how atmosphere (not just coffee) drives brand value and customer experience
Cannibalization: evaluate impact on existing high-margin frozen coffees and baked goods
Operational feasibility: freezer storage requirements, store renovation costs, seating space trade-offs, new supplier relationships
Recommendation: deliver a definitive 30-second verdict with clear rationale

questions.prompt: Should Starbucks add ice cream to its retail stores? Walk through your analysis.
questions.guidance: Strong answers cover: (1) Customer mismatch — Starbucks skews higher-income adults seeking a premium atmosphere, while ice cream's primary consumers include children who would disrupt that experience. (2) Cannibalization risk — frozen coffees and baked goods already carry high margins; ice cream could erode those sales without adding equivalent profit. (3) Operational barriers — current stores lack freezer infrastructure, so rollout requires costly renovations that would also reduce seating area. (4) Supplier complexity — adding ice cream likely means onboarding a new supplier and managing cold-chain logistics. Candidate should conclude that Starbucks should NOT add ice cream and deliver a clear 30-second recommendation.

questions.prompt: Given that Starbucks should not sell ice cream in stores, what should they do to grow? Organize your ideas into categories.
questions.guidance: Interviewer is looking for (1) Creativity and (2) Organization — candidates must categorize ideas, not just list them. Key categories and examples: Product innovation — introduce a non-specialty/everyday coffee at a lower price point (e.g., Pike Place Roast) to compete with Dunkin Donuts during tough economic times; sell Starbucks-branded ice cream through retail grocery channels rather than in-store. Geographic expansion — expand into additional suburban and semi-rural areas domestically; pursue selective international city expansion.

brainstorming.prompt: What should Starbucks do to grow, if not add ice cream to stores? Organize your ideas into categories.

categories.name: New Products
ideas: Introduce a non-specialty everyday coffee (e.g., Pike Place Roast) at a lower price to compete with Dunkin Donuts
Sell Starbucks-branded ice cream in retail grocery channels (not in-store)

categories.name: Geographic Expansion
ideas: Expand into additional suburban and semi-rural areas domestically

recommendation: Starbucks should NOT add ice cream to its retail stores

The core Starbucks brand equity rests on a premium atmosphere for adult coffee drinkers; ice cream would attract children, disrupt that atmosphere, cannibalize high-margin frozen beverages and baked goods, and require costly store renovations with no clear profit upside
risks: Continued competitive pressure from Dunkin Donuts / Baskin Robbins partnership if Starbucks does not respond with some growth initiative
Risk of brand dilution if Starbucks pursues the wrong adjacency
next_steps: Explore lower-price-point coffee offering to defend against Dunkin Donuts on value
Evaluate retail grocery channel for Starbucks-branded packaged ice cream as a separate revenue stream without disrupting store atmosphere
Identify priority international cities for selective expansion
